brief: Bitwise argues Solana's parallel execution and fast block propagation let it process the most transactions of any major chain at near-zero median cost, but a small share of "ordering value" transactions (priority fees and tips) generates most revenue, similar to Google's ad model. This fee capture, plus an app ecosystem that now keeps most combined revenue, makes Solana platform-like rather than a commoditized exchange, the bank argues. Tokenized real-world stocks are still tiny (about $3.3bn versus $152tn of listed equity value) but growing fast, and Solana already leads tokenized-equity trading share. Bitwise builds a 2031 valuation on projected transaction volume by category, a revenue multiple (40x base case, versus Solana's current 230x), and a 20% discount rate, yielding bear/base/bull price outlooks of $80/$385/$1,100. It flags regulation, competitors capturing ordering value offchain, scaling requirements, competition from Ethereum/Robinhood/Base, and model-input uncertainty as risks to the thesis.
